page: OVHcloud c2-7 is a KVM-based compute-optimized server instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Haswell architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz, the processor lacks TSX instructions but includes AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA flags. The hardware configuration is bundled with 7.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.5 GB per core, alongside 50 GB of local SSD storage and a single complimentary public IPv4 address. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers relative to modern hardware. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU evaluations score in the bottom 10%, reflecting the older Haswell architecture. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor results, with read-only large block transfers registering at 20.03 GB/sec and write operations at 16.03 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and static web serving throughput fall into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. However, the instance achieves an average text generation speed of 74.86 tokens/sec during LLM inference testing with a small 135M model, though prompt processing remains weak at 212.61 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2-7 offers dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading at an entry-level resource density, making it a predictable option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without the risk of noisy neighbors. The primary tradeoff is the reliance on legacy Intel hardware, which limits its computational throughput and memory speeds compared to contemporary architectures. This server is best suited for lightweight general-purpose tasks, basic web serving, small-scale database operations, and low-intensity background processing that benefit from dedicated CPU execution but do not require high memory bandwidth or modern vector instruction sets.
